meta.description: Machine-readable concept taxonomy aligned with the SimpleL7Proxy source code and documentation. Not intended for human consumption.

domains.name: Request Lifecycle
domains.description: End-to-end path a request travels from client to backend and back.

domains.name: Backend Management
domains.description: How the proxy discovers, probes, and selects backend hosts.

domains.name: Reliability
domains.description: Mechanisms that prevent failures from propagating to clients.

domains.name: Request Governance
domains.description: Validation and priority rules applied before a request enters the queue.

domains.name: Async Mode
domains.description: Long-running request handling that decouples client wait from backend processing.

domains.name: Observability
domains.description: How the proxy exposes telemetry about its own operation.

domains.name: Configuration Management
domains.description: How settings reach the proxy and when they take effect.

domains.name: Authentication and Security
domains.description: How the proxy authenticates to backends and restricts inbound callers.

domains.name: Deployment Architecture
domains.description: How the proxy is packaged and run on Azure.

domains.name: Protocol and Headers
domains.description: Named HTTP signals that cross the client-proxy and proxy-backend boundaries.

concepts.name: Listener
concepts.definition: Accepts inbound HTTP connections and submits each request to the priority queue.

concepts.name: RequestData
concepts.definition: Runtime object holding all data for one inbound request: headers, body, path, assigned priority, and TTL expiry.

concepts.name: Request Lifecycle Manager
concepts.definition: Coordinates request state transitions, TTL expiry, completion, failure, and cleanup across synchronous and asynchronous processing.

concepts.name: Request Types
concepts.definition: Execution modes used to route responses and background work.

concepts.name: Enqueue
concepts.definition: Submitting a RequestData into the priority queue. The TTL clock starts at this moment.

concepts.name: Max Queue Length
concepts.definition: Hard cap on queued requests. Requests arriving when the queue is full receive 429 Too Many Requests.

concepts.name: Priority Queue
concepts.definition: Sorted list ordered by priority level integer using binary-search insertion. Lower integer exits first.

concepts.name: Priority Level
concepts.definition: Integer assigned to every request. Lower number means higher dispatch precedence in the queue.

concepts.name: Default Priority
concepts.definition: Priority level assigned when the request carries no matching PriorityKeyHeader value.

concepts.name: TTL (Time-to-Live)
concepts.definition: Wall-clock budget for the entire request lifecycle covering queue wait plus all retry attempts. Expiry returns 412.

concepts.name: ProxyWorker
concepts.definition: Worker loop that dequeues a request and drives the backend selection, send, and response write cycle.

concepts.name: Workers
concepts.definition: Count of concurrent proxy workers. Cold setting; default 10 is for local testing only.

concepts.name: ProxyData
concepts.definition: Runtime object holding a backend response: HTTP status code, response headers, and body.

concepts.name: Pass-through
concepts.definition: Any backend status code in AcceptableStatusCodes is forwarded directly to the client without triggering retry or circuit recording.

concepts.name: Injected Response Headers
concepts.definition: HTTP headers the proxy appends to every successfully proxied response before returning to the client.

concepts.name: Backend Host
concepts.definition: A single upstream endpoint the proxy can forward requests to. Configured as Host1 through Host9.

concepts.name: Connection String Format
concepts.definition: Preferred per-host configuration using a semicolon-delimited key=value string. Only this format supports path, mode, usemi, processor, and other modern options.

concepts.name: Legacy Format
concepts.definition: Deprecated per-variable host configuration. Cannot express path, mode, usemi, or other modern per-host options. Must not be used in new deployments.

concepts.name: Path Prefix
concepts.definition: URL prefix configured on a host via the path connection string key. Requests whose URL starts with this prefix are routed to this host.

concepts.name: Catch-all Host
concepts.definition: A host with path=/ or no path configured. Receives requests that match no specific-path host.

concepts.name: IP Override
concepts.definition: Forces all requests to a specific IP address, bypassing DNS resolution for that host.

concepts.name: Strip Prefix
concepts.definition: When true (default), the matched path prefix is removed from the URL before forwarding. Set stripprefix=false to preserve the full original path.

concepts.name: Processor
concepts.definition: Named stream processor applied to the backend response after receipt. The built-in OpenAI processor extracts token usage counts from SSE streams.

concepts.name: Stream Processor Factory
concepts.definition: Selects and creates response stream processors by configured name, TOKENPROCESSOR response header, and media type, with DefaultStream fallback.

concepts.name: Direct Mode
concepts.definition: Backend mode where the host is always treated as healthy. No probe is ever sent. In latency mode the host sorts first (0 ms average latency). Use for serverless or on-demand backends that must not be woken by probes.

concepts.name: Health Poller
concepts.definition: Background loop that probes each configured host at PollInterval ms intervals and tracks rolling success rate and average latency.

concepts.name: Probe Path
concepts.definition: URL path sent as a GET request to test backend health. Ignored when mode=direct.

concepts.name: Success Rate
concepts.definition: Rolling percentage of successful probe responses for a host. Hosts below the SuccessRate threshold are removed from the active pool until they recover.

concepts.name: Active Pool
concepts.definition: Set of backend hosts currently eligible to receive traffic, filtered by rolling success rate threshold.

concepts.name: Average Latency
concepts.definition: Rolling average probe response time per host. Used to order hosts in latency load-balance mode. Direct-mode hosts report 0 ms and sort first.

concepts.name: BaseHostHealth
concepts.definition: Runtime object holding a single host's health metrics: rolling success rate, average latency, and circuit breaker state.

concepts.name: Backend Selection Pipeline
concepts.definition: Three-stage process run on every request: (1) path filter, (2) load-balance ordering, (3) per-host circuit-breaker gate.

concepts.name: IteratorFactory
concepts.definition: Creates a load-balance iterator for a given request path based on LoadBalanceMode configuration.

concepts.name: Path Filter
concepts.definition: Stage 1 of backend selection. Specific-path hosts are checked first; if none match, catch-all hosts are used. Specific paths always win.

concepts.name: Load Balance Mode
concepts.definition: Stage 2 of backend selection. Determines the ordering of hosts within the matched set for each request.

concepts.name: Round-Robin Iterator
concepts.definition: Distributes requests evenly across active hosts using a global atomic counter.

concepts.name: Latency Iterator
concepts.definition: Orders hosts by ascending average probe latency per request. Direct-mode hosts always sort first at 0 ms.

concepts.name: Random Iterator
concepts.definition: Shuffles active hosts randomly on each request, producing no predictable access pattern.

concepts.name: Shared Iterator
concepts.definition: Single iterator shared across all concurrent requests to the same path. Enables strict round-robin fairness across parallel workers.

concepts.name: Iteration Mode
concepts.definition: Controls retry breadth. SinglePass tries each host at most once. MultiPass cycles through all hosts until MaxAttempts is reached; set MaxAttempts to 0 to disable the cap.

concepts.name: Max Attempts
concepts.definition: Maximum total host attempts in MultiPass mode. Set to 0 to disable the attempt-count limit. Hosts skipped because their circuit is OPEN do not consume an attempt.

concepts.name: Circuit Breaker
concepts.definition: Per-host failure counter with a sliding time window. Opens when the failure count in the window reaches CBErrorThreshold.

concepts.name: CLOSED State
concepts.definition: Normal circuit breaker state. Requests are forwarded to the host.

concepts.name: OPEN State
concepts.definition: Circuit tripped. Host is skipped by the load-balance iterator. Skipped hosts do not consume the MaxAttempts budget.

concepts.name: Sliding Window
concepts.definition: Only failures timestamped within the last CBTimeslice seconds count toward the threshold. Older entries are pruned automatically.

concepts.name: Auto-Recovery
concepts.definition: Circuit closes automatically when all failures age out of the sliding window. No manual intervention required.

concepts.name: Progressive Delay
concepts.definition: Artificial per-request delay (100-500 ms) added as a host's failure count approaches CBErrorThreshold. Not configurable.

concepts.name: Global Blocked Check
concepts.definition: Static circuit-breaker registry check that reports whether all registered circuit breakers are OPEN. The current request path does not call this helper directly.

concepts.name: Acceptable Status Codes
concepts.definition: HTTP status codes from backends that are not counted as circuit-breaker failures and are forwarded to the client.

concepts.name: Retry
concepts.definition: Advancing to the next host in the iterator after a non-acceptable backend response. Does not apply when the circuit is OPEN.

concepts.name: Requeue
concepts.definition: Returning a request to the priority queue after host attempts are exhausted and at least one backend returned 429 with S7PREQUEUE:true. Uses the shortest requeue delay seen.

concepts.name: S7PREQUEUE
concepts.definition: Response header a backend sets on a 429 reply to make the request eligible for delayed requeue after the proxy finishes trying available hosts.

concepts.name: Retry-After
concepts.definition: Delay from retry-after-ms (milliseconds) or Retry-After (seconds), defaulting to 1000 ms. The proxy uses the shortest eligible delay seen after host attempts are exhausted.

concepts.name: Timeout
concepts.definition: Per-host-attempt window in milliseconds. Resets on each retry. Effective deadline per attempt = min(remaining TTL, Timeout).

concepts.name: AsyncTriggerTimeout
concepts.definition: Milliseconds after enqueue before the proxy releases the client with a 202 response and continues processing in the background.

concepts.name: AsyncTimeout
concepts.definition: Maximum backend processing time in milliseconds once a request is in async mode.

concepts.name: AsyncTTLSecs
concepts.definition: Request TTL in seconds applied when async processing starts, replacing the synchronous request expiration.

concepts.name: Validation Pipeline
concepts.definition: Ordered sequence of validation checks applied to every non-probe inbound request before it is enqueued. The execution order is fixed.

steps.when: ValidateAuthConfig enables key, oauth2, or mixed mode

concepts.name: App ID Validation
concepts.definition: Step 2 of the validation pipeline when enabled. Checks the caller's Entra Application ID against a remote allowlist before header stripping and profile/header validation checks. Designed for deployments with more than 13 App IDs (Entra's built-in limit).

concepts.name: Inbound Key Validation
concepts.definition: Step 1 optional auth gate. In key or mixed mode, the proxy checks the configured inbound header against ValidateAuthKey1 or ValidateAuthKey2; bearer values in oauth2 or mixed mode use token validation.

concepts.name: Inbound OAuth Validation
concepts.definition: Validates inbound bearer tokens in oauth2 or mixed mode using configured issuer, audience, lifetime, signature, required claims, and clock-skew rules.

concepts.name: Request Preprocessor Plugins
concepts.definition: Configured IRequestPreprocessorPlugin implementations invoked before request validation and enqueue. The allow-all implementation is used when no valid plugin is configured.

concepts.name: Header Stripping
concepts.definition: Step 3 of the validation pipeline. Removes headers listed in DisallowedHeaders silently. No error is returned to the caller.

concepts.name: Required Headers
concepts.definition: List of header names that must be non-empty on every request. The first missing header returns 417.

concepts.name: Disallowed Headers
concepts.definition: Headers stripped silently from the request before forwarding. Automatically includes the allowlist header when ValidateHeaders is configured.

concepts.name: Header Validation Rule
concepts.definition: ValidateHeaders mapping SourceHeader=AllowlistHeader. The source header value must appear in the comma-separated allowlist header injected from the user profile. Supports * suffix for prefix matching.
side_effects: auto-adds SourceHeader and AllowlistHeader to RequiredHeaders

concepts.name: App ID Allowlist
concepts.definition: File or URL returning the list of permitted Entra Application IDs. Enforced at step 2 of the validation pipeline.

concepts.name: User Profile
concepts.definition: Per-user JSON object loaded periodically from a URL or file. Drives priority assignment, async configuration, and custom header injection.

profile_fields.description: Unique identifier matched against the incoming request header.
Priority tier value mapped via PriorityKeys.
Enables async mode and sets per-user blob container and Service Bus topic.
Any other key is injected as an HTTP request header.

concepts.name: User ID
concepts.definition: Unique identifier extracted from a configurable request header and used to look up the user profile record.

concepts.name: S7PPriorityKey Profile Field
concepts.definition: User profile field whose value is matched against PriorityKeys to assign a priority tier to the user's requests.

concepts.name: async-config Profile Field
concepts.definition: User profile field enabling async mode for a specific user. Specifies the user's blob container name and Service Bus topic.
concepts.behavior_note: generatesas is parsed and retained, but the current blob URI path returns base URIs and does not generate SAS tokens.

concepts.name: Profile Refresh
concepts.definition: Proxy reloads the user profile file at the configured interval (default 1 hour). Enables live user management without restart.

concepts.name: Suspended User
concepts.definition: User whose ID appears in the suspended users list. Returns 403 immediately, regardless of profile content.

concepts.name: Priority Mapping
concepts.definition: Maps a request header value to an internal priority integer and allocates dedicated worker threads to that priority level.
concepts.constraint: Count of PriorityKeys MUST equal count of PriorityValues. PriorityWorkers MUST reference only levels in PriorityValues.

concepts.name: Priority Key Header
concepts.definition: Name of the request header the proxy inspects to determine priority tier. Default: S7PPriorityKey.

concepts.name: Priority Keys
concepts.definition: Comma-separated list of expected header values. Each entry maps 1:1 to the corresponding entry in PriorityValues.

concepts.name: Priority Values
concepts.definition: Comma-separated list of internal priority integers, in 1:1 correspondence with PriorityKeys.

concepts.name: Priority Workers
concepts.definition: PriorityLevel:WorkerCount pairs that reserve dedicated worker threads for each priority level.

concepts.name: Per-user Throttling
concepts.definition: When a user's active requests exceed UserPriorityThreshold as a fraction of the total queue, that user's new requests are deprioritized.

concepts.name: Async Mode
concepts.definition: System-wide feature enabling asynchronous request processing. Must be enabled at three levels: proxy (AsyncModeEnabled), user profile (async-config field), and per-request (opt-in header).

concepts.name: Opt-in Header
concepts.definition: Per-request header clients send to request async processing for that call. Default header name: S7PAsyncMode.

concepts.name: Async Upgrade
concepts.definition: After AsyncTriggerTimeout ms, the proxy returns 202 to the client containing blob URIs and continues backend processing in the background.

concepts.name: 202 Accepted Response
concepts.definition: HTTP 202 returned after async upgrade. The JSON body and x-Data-Blob-URI and x-Header-Blob-URI response headers identify the result blobs.

concepts.name: Result Blob
concepts.definition: Azure Blob Storage object written when the backend completes an async request. Its base URI is included in the 202 response body and headers.

concepts.name: Blob Lifecycle Policy
concepts.definition: External Azure Storage lifecycle management rule used to delete result blobs. The proxy does not configure or enforce blob deletion.

concepts.name: Service Bus Status
concepts.definition: Real-time async lifecycle events sent to a per-user Azure Service Bus topic as requests move through processing states.

concepts.name: Status Events
concepts.definition: Lifecycle notification values sent over Service Bus.

concepts.name: Async Blob Worker
concepts.definition: Background thread that writes completed async request results to Azure Blob Storage.

concepts.name: Async Worker
concepts.definition: Coordinates async upgrade, client 202 release, blob response streams, status events, and request recovery state.

concepts.name: Request API
concepts.definition: Azure Functions subsystem backed by Cosmos DB that records, checks, and re-feeds asynchronous and background request state.

concepts.name: Streaming Microservice
concepts.definition: HTTP-triggered Azure Function that streams an upstream URL through a selected stream processor and emits processor statistics to Application Insights.

concepts.name: ProxyEvent
concepts.definition: Key/value dictionary capturing all dimensions of a single proxied request: HTTP status, timing, token counts, headers, and other metadata.

concepts.name: Event Headers
concepts.definition: Common fields injected into every ProxyEvent: application version, container name, and revision. Supplied by the ICommonEventData implementation.

concepts.name: CompositeEventClient
concepts.definition: Fan-out dispatcher that sends every serialized ProxyEvent to all registered event logger backends. Uses FrozenDictionary for zero-lock dispatch on the hot path.

concepts.name: Event Logger Backend
concepts.definition: Named sink that receives serialized JSON ProxyEvents. Built-in values are file and eventhub; none disables event sinks. Custom backends implement IEventClient and optionally IHostedService.

concepts.name: Custom Event Logger
concepts.definition: User-supplied IEventClient selected by fully qualified type name. IHostedService implementations are also started by the host and can self-register with CompositeEventClient.

concepts.name: Application Insights
concepts.definition: Primary production telemetry sink. Receives structured telemetry (requests, dependencies, exceptions) via TelemetryClient.

concepts.name: Event Hubs
concepts.definition: High-volume streaming telemetry sink for JSON event lines. Supports connection-string auth or Managed Identity.

concepts.name: Log File
concepts.definition: Local JSON-lines file sink for development and testing. Buffers events and flushes at 10 events or every 2 seconds.

concepts.name: Token Telemetry
concepts.definition: Prompt and completion token counts extracted from SSE (Server-Sent Events) streams and logged per request. Requires processor=OpenAI on the backend host.

concepts.name: /liveness Endpoint
concepts.definition: Returns 200 OK if the process is running. Never returns 503.

concepts.name: /readiness Endpoint
concepts.definition: Returns 200 when startup is complete, hosts are active and healthy, event backlog is within limits, and the async blob queue is healthy; otherwise returns 503.

responses.503: startup, host, event backlog, or blob queue health criteria failed

concepts.name: /startup Endpoint
concepts.definition: Returns 200 when the proxy is initialized and the same host, event backlog, and blob queue health criteria used for readiness are satisfied; otherwise returns 503.

concepts.name: Sidecar Mode
concepts.definition: Isolation pattern where a separate HealthProbe container on port 9000 handles Kubernetes probes. The proxy pushes its health state to the sidecar every second. If no update arrives for 10 seconds the sidecar fails probes.

concepts.name: Health Probe Implementations
concepts.definition: Interchangeable .NET and Python sidecar servers exposing liveness, readiness, startup, and internal status-update endpoints on HEALTHPROBE_PORT.

concepts.name: Warm Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration value hot-reloaded from Azure App Configuration within ~30 seconds when the Sentinel key changes. No container restart required.

concepts.name: Cold Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration value published to Azure App Configuration but taking effect only after a container restart.

concepts.name: Hidden Setting
concepts.definition: Configuration value never published to Azure App Configuration. Runtime-derived from composite connection strings or infrastructure state.

concepts.name: Sentinel
concepts.definition: Special key (Warm:Sentinel) in Azure App Configuration. Bumping its value to any new value triggers hot-reload of all Warm settings across all running proxy instances.

concepts.name: Composite Connection String
concepts.definition: Semicolon or comma-delimited key=value string encoding multiple related settings in one environment variable.

concepts.name: App Configuration Label
concepts.definition: Label filter applied when reading from Azure App Configuration. Allows isolated setting namespaces per environment.

concepts.name: Refresh Interval
concepts.definition: How often in seconds the proxy polls the Sentinel key in Azure App Configuration.

concepts.name: Stream Flush Interval
concepts.definition: Cold setting in milliseconds that controls how often StreamFlusher runs and flushes tracked active response streams.

concepts.name: Configuration Plugin
concepts.definition: Startup extension selected by EnvPluginClass that supplies environment-specific configuration overrides before the proxy services are registered.

concepts.name: Managed Identity
concepts.definition: Azure-managed credential attached to the container. Used for keyless authentication to backends, App Configuration, Event Hubs, Blob Storage, and Service Bus.

concepts.name: OAuth2 Bearer Token
concepts.definition: Proxy acquires an Entra ID token and attaches it as Authorization: Bearer on outbound backend requests.

concepts.name: Keyless Auth
concepts.definition: Configuration pattern using usemi=true and audience=https://cognitiveservices.azure.com to eliminate API key management for Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry backends.

concepts.name: VNet Deployment
concepts.definition: Deployment pattern where the proxy runs entirely inside a Virtual Network with no external data plane dependencies. Supports sovereign and government cloud regions.

concepts.name: Azure Container Apps
concepts.definition: Primary hosting platform for SimpleL7Proxy. Provides ingress, auto-scaling, managed identity, and revision management.

concepts.name: Container Image
concepts.definition: Docker image pushed to Azure Container Registry (ACR) and deployed to Azure Container Apps.

concepts.name: Sidecar Deployment
concepts.definition: Two-container ACA revision: proxy container on port 8000 and health probe container on port 9000. Both containers share localhost networking within the revision.

concepts.name: Parameters File
concepts.definition: Local parameter file consumed by the VNet provisioning script for Azure target, network, and subnet values.

concepts.name: APIM Integration
concepts.definition: Azure API Management as a front-end to SimpleL7Proxy. Adds semantic caching, PII scrubbing, TPM-based rate limiting, quota enforcement, and mTLS.

concepts.name: AI Foundry Integration
concepts.definition: Direct or APIM-mediated connection to Azure OpenAI and AI Foundry model endpoints. Requires processor=OpenAI for token count extraction.

response_codes.name: Accepted
response_codes.cause: Async upgrade: client released early with blob URIs

response_codes.name: Forbidden
response_codes.cause: App ID not in allowlist (DisallowedAppID); inbound key validation failed (DisallowedKey); user not in profile or suspended (UnknownProfile)

response_codes.name: Request Timeout
response_codes.cause: IO exception or task cancellation on backend communication

response_codes.name: Expectation Failed
response_codes.cause: Required header missing (IncompleteHeaders); header validation rule failed (InvalidHeader)

response_codes.name: Too Many Requests
response_codes.cause: Queue full; backend circuit check failed; no active hosts; max undrained events exceeded

response_codes.name: Internal Server Error
response_codes.cause: Unhandled exception; request body too large (ContentTooLarge)

response_codes.name: Bad Gateway
response_codes.cause: Backend attempts failed with different status codes or an unclassified transport error

response_codes.name: Service Unavailable
response_codes.cause: No host was attempted or backend name-resolution/connection failures exhausted the available hosts

request_headers.name: S7PPriorityKey
request_headers.definition: Priority tier value. Looked up in PriorityKeys to determine the request's priority level.

request_headers.name: S7PTTL
request_headers.definition: Per-request TTL override in seconds. Formats: integer, decimal, absolute Unix timestamp, ISO 8601.

request_headers.name: S7PTimeout
request_headers.definition: Per-request per-host timeout override in milliseconds.

request_headers.name: S7P-Iterator
request_headers.definition: Per-request iteration mode override. Accepted values: SinglePass and MultiPass. Missing or invalid values use the current IterationMode default.

request_headers.name: S7PAsyncMode
request_headers.definition: Opt-in header enabling async mode for this specific request.

request_headers.name: S7PDEBUG
request_headers.definition: Set to true to enable per-request debug tracing in logs.

request_headers.name: S7PREQUEUE
request_headers.definition: Set by a backend on a 429 response to signal the proxy should requeue the request.

request_headers.name: retry-after-ms
request_headers.definition: Preferred backend requeue delay in milliseconds.

request_headers.name: Retry-After
request_headers.definition: Backend requeue delay in seconds, used when retry-after-ms is absent.

response_headers.name: Request-Queue-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds the request spent in the priority queue before a worker picked it up on successful responses.

response_headers.name: Request-Process-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds spent in the proxy worker from dequeue to final response write on successful responses.

response_headers.name: BackendHost
response_headers.definition: Hostname of the backend that served the successful response.

response_headers.name: Total-Latency
response_headers.definition: Total milliseconds from enqueue to response complete on successful responses.

response_headers.name: Attempts
response_headers.definition: Backend attempts made during the current dispatch cycle.

response_headers.name: Lifetime-Attempts
response_headers.definition: Cumulative backend attempts across all requeue cycles.

response_headers.name: x-Request-Queue-Duration
response_headers.definition: Milliseconds spent in the priority queue on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-Total-Latency
response_headers.definition: Total milliseconds from enqueue to an exhausted-host error response.

response_headers.name: x-ProxyHost
response_headers.definition: Proxy hostname included on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-MID
response_headers.definition: Message identifier included on exhausted-host error responses.

response_headers.name: x-Data-Blob-URI
response_headers.definition: Async response data blob URI returned with a 202 Accepted response.

response_headers.name: x-Header-Blob-URI
response_headers.definition: Async response header blob URI returned with a 202 Accepted response.

relationships.description: TTL caps total request lifetime; Timeout caps each individual attempt.
AsyncTriggerTimeout fires first to release the client; AsyncTimeout governs the subsequent backend phase.
Path filter runs before load-balance ordering in the backend selection pipeline.
Load balancer orders hosts; circuit breaker gates each host before attempt.
Health poller results determine which hosts are in the active pool.
Active pool hosts are also subject to per-host circuit breaker evaluation.
OPEN circuits are skipped without consuming a MaxAttempts budget entry.
Bumping Sentinel triggers hot-reload of all Warm settings.
Validation pipeline must pass before a request is enqueued.
User profile supplies the allowlist header values consumed by header validation rules.
Async upgrade initiates background processing that ultimately produces a result blob.
Result blobs are deleted by the Azure Storage lifecycle policy, not by the proxy setting alone.
processor=OpenAI is required for the proxy to extract token counts from SSE streams.
CompositeEventClient fans out every ProxyEvent to all registered backends.
Connection string format supports all modern options; legacy format is deprecated.
Direct-mode hosts report 0 ms average latency and always sort first in latency mode.
